$comment: Machine-readable mirror of src/styles/globals.css. That file is the source of truth; if the two disagree, the CSS wins.
name: Limbo Mixology

display.source: Google Fonts, self-hosted at build time

body.source: Google Fonts, self-hosted at build time. Variable 400-700, true tabular figures.
body.usage: all body copy, labels, UI text

typography.$note: T3 as built, §39. The previous note here read 'There is no sans-serif in this product. Both faces are serif, deliberately.' Sean withdrew that rule on 11 Sep — 'I'm no longer concerned with the sans-serif rule' — and then picked T3, whose body face is a sans. Kept and marked rather than deleted, because the rule was real and the reason it went is worth knowing.
typography.$retired: Eyesome (display, purchased, self-hosted) and Radley (body). Retiring Eyesome changed two shipped call sites — Wordmark.tsx and the login screen's 48px 'Limbo Mixology', which is the first thing a client sees. The .otf files are kept but no longer loaded.
typography.$owed: Two numbers were set by device test against Radley and need re-testing on the iPad under Instrument Sans: the 61px list row (measures 61px in Chrome on the Mac, unverified on device) and the 13px floor, which may safely drop now that the body face is a sans.

sectionLabel.$note: bigger AND tighter — wide tracking at 10-12px pulls letters apart until the word loses its silhouette and has to be read letter by letter

rowTitle.$note: leading explicit — at `normal` the 61px row lands at 66.5px and the phone drawer's fourth add row stops fitting

invoiceTotal.$note: every width, no responsive exception — measured 92.8px to 145.9px in Radley 600

typography.$scaleRule: x1.25 on everything that carries content, floor 13px. A desk monitor sits at ~450-500mm; an iPad held standing sits at ~550-650mm, so type must scale with viewing distance to hold the same angular size. Dim venues cost more: a dilated pupil has worse acuity and Radley is a fine-stroked serif. It is the same argument that produced the 44px touch target, applied to reading instead of touch. Frame 14A, applied 2 Aug 2026.
typography.$floor: 13px. Nothing smaller anywhere, in any state, including disabled and placeholder text.

$notes: Palette 3A plus the round-3 corrections (handoff 31 Jul, sections 1.3 and 1.4).
NAMES: globals.css owns them. Design's round-2 ramp renamed --surface-sunken and --text-secondary; round 3 retracted that. Reverted, and Design's handed-over markup uses the original names.
Set a token against the DARKEST surface it appears on. In dark that is --surface-recessed.

--accent and --accent-surface are SEPARATE and must stay so. --accent does two jobs: a dark fill carrying light text in light mode, and a legible foreground in dark, so it lifts. --accent-surface is chrome and stays deep in both. Conflating them broke dark mode in round 2.
Dark --accent reverted to #7FA894 with --accent-fg #14120E (7.1:1). The ramp's #4A7A6A failed AA against both candidates (4.24:1 / 3.82:1).
--accent-fg is #FFFFFF in light. Legal: the no-pure-white rule governs backgrounds, not foregrounds.
--gold is fills, borders and underlines ONLY, never type, in either mode. The active tab's edge is 3px --accent for that reason (9.27:1 vs gold's 2.6-3.1:1).
--surface-recessed (#E1DACA light) is the inactive tab fill. --border-strong is the stage control's button borders.

radius.$note: Semantic, by component role — so 'make cards less rounded' is one edit and cannot reshape badges by accident.

elevation.$note: X2 as built, §39. Theme-dependent — light-mode shadows are invisible on a dark background. The border still does the separation work; the shadow sits ON the hairline and never replaces it.
elevation.$rule: Light shadows are rgba(52,38,20,*), the palette's own brown, NEVER rgba(0,0,0,*). §36.4 objected that a soft shadow on warm cream turns to mud; §39.1 found the objection was about a NEUTRAL shadow and reversed it. Dark keeps black — there is no cream at #1A1712, and a shadow lighter than its ground is a glow.

$roles.card: two parts — a contact shadow that sits the card on the ground, a wide one that lifts it off
$roles.control: buttons and the active segment. Pressable, not stacked: contact and no lift. NOT the card value made smaller.
$roles.bar: the one shadow that points UP. A fixed bar at the bottom of a list separates itself from content above it.

spacing.$note: Tailwind 4 default scale. Every padding and gap is a multiple, so the whole layout tightens from one value.

layout.$note: TWO breakpoints, settled 1 Aug 2026 in handoff 5.1.1. 600px separates phone geometry from tablet portrait; 1024px separates portrait from landscape. 600 and not 768: an iPad mini in portrait is 744px CSS, so a 768 boundary put an 8.3-inch tablet on phone geometry. 600 sits ~160px clear of the largest phone and ~144px clear of the smallest tablet, and is Material's compact-to-medium boundary.

below.header: brand lockup, search icon, settings; slides away on scroll down

atOrAbove.navigation: left sidebar, 240px, collapsible to a 64px icon rail

ranges.<600px: single column, drawer over the invoice (handoff 5.1)
ranges.600-1023px: portrait tablet, drawer under a full invoice (handoff 5)

touch.$note: Non-negotiable. Used standing up with hands full.
touch.minInputFontSizeReason: anything smaller makes iOS Safari zoom on focus
rules: No hover-only interactions, ever. A finger has no hover.
Safe area insets on anything at a screen edge.
Pointer Events, not touch or mouse events — one path covers finger, Apple Pencil, and cursor.
platformLimits: No haptics available in Safari. Gestures must confirm themselves visually.
Apple Pencil hover works on newer iPads but can never be the only route to an action.

antiPatterns: Pure black or neutral grey in dark mode
Grids of large cards for long lists — use rows, for density
